subject: Intermittent 429 surge at peak — credit eligibility & RCA timeline
messages:
From: Maya Simmons <maya@stratafin.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@stratafin.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike of 429s during Monday peak window — can you confirm eligibility?

Hi Ben,

We saw a sharp spike in 429 responses to our inference calls on Monday (May 3) between 09:15–09:24 PDT. This affected several customer-facing pipelines — roughly ~12% of calls during that 9-minute window returned 429 and a number of batches timed out. Our internal SLA with Redwood calls out availability and error-rate thresholds; before I open a formal claim with procurement, can you confirm whether this meets Redwood's SLA credit criteria and whether you can provide an initial logs bundle?

Key details from our side:
- Region: us-west-2 (single-region traffic)
- Peak request QPS: 820 (50ms median latency otherwise)
- Error type: 429 throttling + some 504 timeouts downstream
- Internal impact: briefly degraded feature availability, mitigation via client-side retry/backoff

We need:
1) Confirmation of Redwood-observed error window and error rate
2) Whether this is eligible for credit under our contract (SF-23847)
3) Timeline for a postmortem and log bundle for audit (SOC-related)

Thanks — this is high priority for our legal/procurement teams.

—Maya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike of 429s during Monday peak window — can you confirm eligibility?

Maya — pulled the initial evidence and attaching a CSV of 1-minute buckets for error counts and a zipped sample of request traces. Preliminary findings below:

Summary of findings (preliminary):
- Observed elevated 429-rate precisely between 09:16:00–09:24:00 PDT (8 full minutes).
- 429 count: 9,840 requests across the customer pool; for StrataFin's tenancy we see ~2,400 of those (consistent with your ~12% figure).
- The spike coincides with a brief autoscaler delay — an influx of new warmed containers lagged by ~18–22s which caused synchronous throttling at the frontend queue.
- Median latency outside window: 48ms; during spike, retry/backoff interactions produced additional 504s at the backend while clients retried.

Attachments included: slo-429-spike.csv (1-min buckets), kpi-sample-logs.zip (sample traces and sampling manifest).

Eligibility note: per our SLA (section 4.2 error-rate availability), this kind of sustained error spike over an SLO window may qualify for a pro-rata credit. We need to run the full eligibility calc (customer's committed availability and the exact SLO measurement window). I'll own the evidence pull and run the eligibility calculation; expect an initial credit estimate by EOD tomorrow.

Next steps:
- I will generate the formal evidence bundle (logs + trace manifests) and upload to the Drive link below.
- We will prepare a preliminary RCA and a proposed corrective action (autoscaler tuning + guardrail on startup parallelism).

Marissa Cole
